title: Processing of identified data during registration
description: The Authentication Service receives and processes identified personal data (e.g. username, email, password) from the Parent User as part of the register action.
assumptions: Registration flows inherently involve some form of account-identifying information to create or authenticate the user account.

title: User unawareness when sharing registration data
description: The Parent User shares personal data for registration without full awareness of how the Authentication Service will process, store or further use that data.
assumptions: Users often do not read or understand privacy policies or data processing details at the time of registration.

title: Collection of sensitive data types for registration
description: Authentication Service collects data types such as passwords or contact information that are sensitive in nature.
assumptions: Passwords and emails are typically required for registration but are inherently sensitive.

title: Processing of identified account data
description: The MongoDB users collection stores account data which includes identified information such as usernames or emails for authentication purposes.
assumptions: Account storage typically requires unique identifiers to function.

title: Sensitive data type storage for accounts
description: Account data stored may include sensitive types like credentials or personal details beyond minimal needs if not carefully scoped.
assumptions: Authentication accounts often involve passwords or equivalent which are sensitive.

title: Account data as attributable evidence
description: Stored account records in the users collection can be used as evidence attributing actions or existence of accounts to specific users.
assumptions: Data records link back to individuals via identifiers.

title: JWT unique identifier enables linking
description: The JWT in the flow contains a unique subject identifier or token ID that can link authentication events to child profile accesses across the system.
assumptions: JWT standard claims like sub or jti are present in the token.

title: JWT carries pseudonym/identifier
description: The authentication JWT transmitted includes a unique reference (e.g., user or child subject claim) allowing identification or re-identification of the data subject at the receiving service.
assumptions: Standard JWT subject claim or similar identifier is included.

title: Sensitive child data in JWT or payload
description: Authentication Service shares JWT plus additional data that may include sensitive child profile attributes beyond what is strictly required for the profile management operation.
assumptions: Child-related data is involved given the destination process name.
uncertainty_note: Flow description mentions 'data' without specifying content; sensitivity inferred from context.

title: Signed JWT prevents repudiation
description: The signed JWT provides attributable evidence of the authentication action and data exchange, preventing the source from denying the transmission or claims within the token.
assumptions: JWT is digitally signed as is standard practice.

title: Processing of identified data for child login
description: The Child Profile Management process requests and processes identified login data (e.g. username or other unique reference) from the child user.

title: Linking child login to profile via unique identifier
description: Login uses a unique identifier that allows the process to link the authentication action and data to the specific child profile.

title: Invalid consent for child personal data processing
description: Child login involves collection and processing of personal data; for minors this requires valid parental/guardian consent which may not be properly obtained or verified in the login flow.
uncertainty_note: Child-specific consent requirements are inferred from context of 'child login' but exact age verification mechanism not specified in flow.

title: Child data subject unaware of processing implications
description: As a child user sharing login data, the data subject may lack full awareness of how their personal data will be collected, stored, or used beyond the immediate login.

title: Identifier in JWT
description: The JWT transmitted in this flow contains a unique reference to the identity of the child data subject.
assumptions: JWT typically includes subject claims or user identifiers.

title: Signed JWT enables attribution
description: The signed JWT in the flow can be used as attributable evidence preventing the child user from denying actions or claims associated with the token.
assumptions: JWTs are digitally signed by default in most implementations.

title: Sensitive child profile data disclosure
description: Child profiles are disclosed via this flow, which may involve highly sensitive personal data of minors.
assumptions: Profiles of children are considered sensitive by nature.
uncertainty_note: Context implies child-related data but exact sensitivity not specified in flow description.

title: Processing of identified child data
description: The Child Profile Management process requests and processes identified personal data about the child to create the profile.

title: Unawareness when sharing child data
description: The parent user shares personal data of the child (data subject) without the child necessarily being aware of the processing.

title: Collection of sensitive child profile data
description: Sensitive personal data types related to a child are collected for profile creation, which may exceed strict functional needs or require extra protections.

title: Potential unlawful processing of child data

title: Sensitive child profile data disclosure

assumptions: Profile data for children is assumed to contain personal and potentially sensitive attributes based on flow name.
uncertainty_note: Exact data fields not specified in flow description, but context implies child personal data.

title: Identified child data in transit

title: Child data subject unawareness

title: Sensitive video data stored

title: Prolonged retention of watch history

title: Child unawareness of processing

title: Child user unaware of video stream receipt and associated processing

description: Metadata in the video stream (e.g., timestamps, quality choices, device info) can be used to profile the child's viewing patterns and link sessions.

title: JWT identifier stored in localStorage

title: Signed JWT prevents deniability
description: The signed JWT stored in localStorage serves as attributable evidence of user actions or authentication claims, preventing the data subject from denying involvement.

title: Broad accessibility of JWT in localStorage
description: Storing the JWT in localStorage makes the authentication token (potentially containing personal data) accessible to any JavaScript running in the browser context, broader than necessary for functionality.
